title: Roster Form and Set-builder Form
subject: Mathematics
objective: Two ways to write one set: Roster form lists the elements, Set-builder form states their common property. When to use each.

fill.q: In roster form, elements are written inside ____ brackets.
The letters of SCHOOL form a set of ____ elements.
In set-builder form, the colon means ____.
The roster form of the vowels is {a, e, i, o, ____}.

tf.q: In roster form an element may be repeated.
An infinite set is best written in set-builder form.
"The tall students of a class" is a set.

ar.a: {a, b} and {b, a} are the same set.
ar.r: The order of elements in a set does not matter.

ar.a: Set-builder form is used for infinite sets.
ar.r: Infinite sets cannot be fully listed.

mcq.q: The letters of BANANA in roster form are:
{x : x is a natural number, x < 4} equals:

mcq.explain: Four even numbers from n = 1 to 4.

num.q: How many elements has {x : x is a prime number, x < 10}?
How many elements has the set of letters of MATHEMATICS?
steps: {M, A, T, H, E, I, C, S}

short.q: Write {x : x is an integer, −3 < x < 2} in roster form.
short.solution: The integers strictly between −3 and 2 are {−2, −1, 0, 1}.
